raw_response:
I farm 4.5 mu here in Quzhou with just me and my wife. My main system is cabbage-eggplant — that's what I've done for years. Last year I had 1.5 mu of cabbage and 1 mu of eggplant, and the remaining 2 mu I split between cauliflower, chili, kidney bean, and spinach. The cabbage gave about 4,000 jin per mu and the eggplant about 3,000 jin. This year I'm keeping the same layout because I know these crops and the dealers at the market here buy them steady.

My neighbor Lao Wang used hybrid cabbage seed last autumn and his heads were much tighter and heavier than mine, so this year I'm switching to hybrid cabbage too. It costs about 80 yuan more per mu for the seed, but if I get even 300 extra jin it pays for itself. I've used hybrid eggplant for five years now, no reason to change. For kidney bean and spinach I still use seed I saved from last year — why spend money when they sprout fine and grow true?

For fertilizer, I start from what I did last year and adjust a little. On the cabbage plot I put down about 100 jin of chicken manure per mu and 80 jin of compound fertilizer as basal dressing. The compound is 15-15-15. Then I top-dress twice with urea, 25 jin each time. That works out to about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu total. The county training class said 15 kg is enough, but I've always done a bit more. Better to waste some fertilizer than have small, loose heads. A bad cabbage harvest is a disaster; wasting 30 yuan on extra urea is just a cost I accept.

The eggplant needs more potassium because it keeps fruiting all summer long. The input dealer told me eggplant is a heavy potassium feeder, so this year I'm adding an extra 20 jin of potassium sulfate on the eggplant mu. My wife's cousin did that last year and his plants stayed healthy and producing into October.

I irrigate from my tube well. Cabbage gets 4 flood irrigations: right after transplanting in late August, at rosette stage, when heads start forming, and about 10 days before harvest so the heads are heavy. Eggplant needs 5 times because July and August are hot and dry here on the North China Plain. Kidney bean and spinach only need 3 times each since they don't sit through the worst heat.

For pesticides, cabbage gets 4 sprays mainly for cabbage worms and aphids. Eggplant gets 5 because spider mites and blight always hit in summer. Cauliflower and chili get 4 each. Spinach only needs 2 sprays since the cold weather keeps most bugs away.

I run the rotary tiller on every plot before planting. No-tillage doesn't work for vegetables — the soil gets too hard, especially after pulling out eggplant roots. Me and my wife do all the labor ourselves. I might hire one person for two days at cabbage transplanting time if the weather window is tight, but that's it. Every yuan I spend on fertilizer is a yuan I don't have for pesticide or hired labor. But I've learned that cutting fertilizer too close is dangerous. I'd rather sleep easy knowing I put down enough than lie awake worrying I cheaped out.
